steps: Drain the tinned fava beans, keeping a splash of the liquid, and tip into a small saucepan.
Add the crushed garlic and cumin and warm over medium heat for 4-5 minutes, mashing about half the beans with a fork for a chunky texture.
Stir in a squeeze of lemon juice and half the olive oil, loosening with a splash of the reserved liquid if it looks dry.
Spoon onto a plate, scatter over the diced tomato and chopped parsley, and drizzle with the remaining olive oil.
Warm the pita for a minute and serve alongside for scooping.
Spread the labneh over a plate or shallow bowl.
Drizzle with olive oil and scatter za'atar over the top.
Slice the cucumber and tomato and arrange them alongside with the olives.
Serve with the pita, torn into pieces for scooping and dipping.
Heat the oil in a frying pan or wok over high heat and add the chopped kimchi, stirring for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Break up the day-old rice with your hands as you add it to the pan, then stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until heated through and starting to catch at the edges.
Add the tamari and sesame oil, tossing to coat evenly, then stir through most of the sliced scallion.
In a separate small pan, fry the egg until the white is set but the yolk stays runny.
Pile the rice onto a plate, top with the fried egg, remaining scallion and shredded nori.
Season the salmon fillet with salt on both sides and grill or pan-sear over medium-high heat for 3-4 minutes per side until it flakes easily.
Meanwhile, bring the dashi to a gentle simmer in a small pan and add the diced tofu and wakame.
Take the pan off the heat and whisk in the miso paste until dissolved — don't let the soup boil again once the miso is in — then cover to keep warm.
Reheat the cooked rice until steaming hot throughout.
Plate the rice and grilled salmon, and serve the miso soup alongside with pickles and a sheet of nori.
Preheat the oven to 200°C and grease a mini muffin tin.
Heat the milk, oil and a pinch of salt in a small pan until just simmering, then pour over the tapioca starch in a bowl and stir until it forms a sticky, stringy dough.
Once cool enough to handle, beat in the eggs one at a time, then mix in the grated cheese until fully combined into a thick batter.
Spoon the batter into the tin, filling each cup about two-thirds full.
Bake for 15-18 minutes until puffed and golden, then cool slightly and serve with sliced banana and coffee.
Rinse the jasmine rice and cook according to packet instructions, then keep warm.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Toss the broccoli florets with a little oil, spread on a baking tray and roast for 15-18 minutes until tender and charred at the edges.
Season the chicken breasts and pan-sear or grill for 6-7 minutes per side until cooked through with no pink in the middle.
Slice the chicken and toss it with the teriyaki sauce and sesame oil in the pan for a minute to glaze.
Divide the rice, roasted broccoli and glazed chicken across containers for the week, or plate straight away.
Rinse the rice and cook according to packet instructions in salted water.
Season the chicken breast with salt on both sides.
Heat the olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 6-7 minutes per side until cooked through and the juices run clear.
Rest the chicken for a couple of minutes, then slice.
Serve the sliced chicken over the rice with extra salt to taste.
Rinse the jasmine rice and cook according to packet instructions.
Season the salmon fillet with salt and a squeeze of lemon, then pan-sear skin-side down for 4-5 minutes, flip and cook a further 2-3 minutes until it flakes easily.
Steam the broccoli, or wilt the spinach, for 4-5 minutes until just tender.
Drizzle the olive oil and remaining lemon juice over the greens.
Plate the rice, salmon and greens together, finishing with a wedge of lemon.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Cut the sweet potato into wedges, toss with a little of the olive oil and roast for 20-25 minutes until a knife goes through easily.
Toss the mixed vegetables with the remaining oil and roast or grill alongside for the last 12-15 minutes until tender and lightly charred.
Season the chicken breast and grill or pan-sear for 6-7 minutes per side until cooked through.
Slice the chicken and plate with the sweet potato wedges and grilled vegetables.
Serve with the cottage cheese on the side.
Rinse the rice and cook according to packet instructions, then keep warm.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Toss the broccoli and carrots with the olive oil and roast for 18-20 minutes until tender and caught at the edges.
Brown the ground beef in a hot pan for 6-8 minutes, breaking it up as it cooks, until no pink remains.
Stir in the taco seasoning and a splash of water, cooking for another minute until the beef is well coated.
Divide the rice, roasted vegetables and beef across containers for the week.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Cut the sweet potato into chunks and toss with half the olive oil on a large baking tray.
Pat the chicken thighs dry, rub with the remaining oil and the paprika, and nestle them among the sweet potato.
Roast for 25 minutes, then add the broccoli florets to the tray.
Return to the oven for a further 12-15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through, with clear juices, and the broccoli is tender.
Rest the chicken for a few minutes before serving straight from the tray, portioning across containers if batching.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Halve the new potatoes and toss on a large baking tray with half the olive oil, the crushed garlic and a few rosemary sprigs.
Roast for 15 minutes while you chop the pepper and courgette into chunks.
Add the chicken thighs, pepper and courgette to the tray and toss with the remaining oil.
Roast for a further 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the potatoes are tender.
Rest briefly before serving, portioning across containers if batching for the week.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Halve the baby potatoes, toss with half the olive oil, and roast for 25-30 minutes until golden and tender.
About 5 minutes before the potatoes are ready, steam or blanch the green beans for 3-4 minutes until just tender.
Bring the steak to room temperature and season well with salt and pepper.
Heat the remaining oil in a hot pan with the crushed garlic and sear the steak for 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare, adjusting to taste.
Rest the steak for a few minutes, then slice and serve with the roasted potatoes and green beans.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Rub the chicken legs with olive oil, season well, and roast for 40-45 minutes until the skin is golden and the juices run clear.
Meanwhile, peel and boil the potatoes in salted water for 15-18 minutes until a knife goes through easily.
Drain the potatoes and mash with the oat milk and a crushed garlic clove until smooth.
For the gravy, warm the chicken stock in a small pan, whisk in the cornstarch mixed with a splash of cold water, and simmer for 2-3 minutes until thickened.
Rest the chicken briefly, then serve with the mash and gravy, portioning across containers if batching.
